title: Equity in Government Compensation Act of 2015
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate passed version is repeated here.)

Equity in Government Compensation Act of 2015

(Sec. 3) This bill requires the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to suspend the compensation packages approved for 2015 for the chief executive officers of the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (government sponsored enterprises or GSEs), and any affiliates, and in lieu of such packages establish the compensation and benefits for each such chief executive officer at the same level in effect for that officer as of January 1, 2015. Such compensation and benefits may not thereafter be increased.

This suspension shall not be construed to affect the prohibition of the STOCK Act against receipt of bonuses by the chief executive officer of each GSE during any period of conservatorship. It shall only apply to such a chief executive officer if the GSE is in conservatorship or receivership as a critically undercapitalized regulated entity pursuant to the Federal Housing Enterprises Financial Safety and Soundness Act of 1992.

(Sec. 4) Any chief executive officer affected by this compensation package suspension shall not be considered a federal employee.

summary.headline: A 2015 law requires the housing regulator to freeze pay for the heads of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac at their January 1, 2015 levels, under certain conservatorship conditions.
summary.what_it_does: The law tells the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency to suspend the 2015 pay packages for the chief executives of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and their affiliates. Their pay and benefits are instead set at the levels they had on January 1, 2015, and they cannot be raised after that. The freeze applies only if the company is in conservatorship or receivership as a critically undercapitalized regulated entity. The law also says these chief executives are not considered federal employees.

who_it_affects.group: Chief executive officers of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and their affiliates
who_it_affects.how: Their pay and benefits are frozen at January 1, 2015 levels, but only if the company is in conservatorship or receivership as a critically undercapitalized entity.

who_it_affects.group: The Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency
who_it_affects.how: The Director must carry out the pay suspension and set the frozen compensation levels.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 25, 2015. The summary does not list a separate start date for the pay provisions.
